summary: Implemented separate work and result-output resource budgets with stable terminal budget codes, explicit incomplete partial semantics and cleanup coverage for text and many-pattern Search execution.

startingState.aheadNote: The ahead count includes reachable completed Search scope commits through W12-S02; no upstream changes were present.

implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning repository's Search production, test and documentation files changed, plus this scope's evidence. No sibling repository, package version, publication state or host/SQL engine source was changed.
implementation.budgetModel: SearchResourceLimits separates eligible input bytes, file bytes, file count, pattern count/size, regex compile cost, record/context bytes, staged output bytes and matcher occurrence count. Shared execution budgets use atomic reservations across parallel workers. Rows are never silently truncated; strict requests fail and the explicit internal partial policy reports an incomplete Partial outcome only after rows were observed.
implementation.cleanupAndDiagnostics: Reader, pooled buffer, sink, pending context and linked cancellation resources remain protected by using/finally boundaries. SearchResourceLimitException carries stable budget codes and terminal summaries report budget-exhausted with countsExact=false.

scenarios: File and total byte budgets expose stable codes and terminal failure summaries.
File-count and dense match-count budgets never truncate as success.
Output cap fails before unbounded staging and disposes the reader.
Literal record-byte budget rejects a huge line and disposes the reader.
Regex physical record limits count decoded non-ASCII bytes.
Pattern, compile and context budgets reject with stable codes.
Explicit partial policy exposes a budget exhaustion as incomplete Partial.

iterationDiagnostics: The review identified that custom regex physical record limits must count decoded bytes rather than UTF-16 characters; a non-ASCII regression test and byte-budget scanner path were added before the final gates.

gateResults.evidence: The exact Release owning-repository suite completed across 21 projects with 1,578 total tests, 1,544 passed, 0 failed and 34 classified skips; the focused Search suite and resource-limit tests also passed.
The separate review approved the budget, failure, cleanup, concurrency and scope behavior; exact source hashes and the unique trailer-bearing completion commit are retained.
Dense match, huge-line, pattern, context, output, file-count, byte-count and explicit-partial cases pass without arbitrary successful truncation; the complete Search suite remains green.
Source, request, completion, match and scope contract harnesses pass 27 scenarios and 314 assertions in total.
Budget failures dispose custom readers and staging state, linked cancellation remains disposed, and atomic shared reservations cover the parallel worker path.

knownLimitations: File and total-byte budgets reserve FileInfo.Length before content processing; this is conservative and does not synchronize concurrent file mutation.
The finite output budget covers Search staging and pending context before writer handoff; existing bounded output channels remain the downstream backpressure boundary.
A cached exact regex pattern reuses its compiled instance without charging a new compilation cost, because no compilation work occurs on that path.
The new limits are exercised through the internal request/options seam; public SQL argument binding remains a later contract boundary.
The repository suite retained 34 classified skips: 31 expected and 3 platform-conditional symlink skips, plus existing package-audit/compiler warnings.
No package was published, pushed, released or installed, and no sibling repository was edited.
